title: The Sunday Roast
story:
Every Sunday, the Hale family gathered at Aunt Rosa's house for a roast dinner. The kitchen windows steamed up while the chicken cooked in the oven. Rosa peeled potatoes and dropped them into a pan of salty water. Her nephew Felix set the table with the blue plates.

At one o'clock the guests arrived. Uncle Martin brought green beans from his garden, and cousin Amina carried a bowl of chopped cabbage. Rosa opened the oven and checked the chicken. The skin was crispy and golden. She lifted it onto a large board and asked Martin to carve. Martin cut even slices and laid them on a warm plate. The smell of herbs filled the room.

Felix made the gravy in the roasting tin. He stirred the brown juices and added the water from the potatoes. Rosa tasted it and asked for a little more pepper. When everything was ready, they sat down together. Amina said the cabbage was sweeter than last week. Martin said the beans were perfect. After the meal, nobody rushed away. They washed the dishes in pairs and talked about the week. Rosa packed leftover chicken into a box for Felix to take home. He promised to have it for lunch on Monday with bread. Before he left, he wrote a shopping list with Rosa for the next Sunday. They needed carrots, more potatoes, and a fresh lemon for the cabbage.
